verdict.summary: You can build a Projects-based OAuth app with the HubSpot CLI and connect your own portal right away, with no review. Without review it installs in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (private) or 25 accounts (Marketplace distribution, after you sign the AUP). Going past 25 means a Marketplace listing, which needs 3 active installs in unrelated companies' accounts and a manual review. The first response comes within 10 business days, and the whole review can take up to 60 days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to reach your own and invited accounts; 1-3 days to prepare a Marketplace listing (docs, policies, shared-data table, domain verification)
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account and for up to 10 (private) or 25 (Marketplace-distribution) installs. Listing review: first response within 10 business days, up to 60 days in total, and it can only start after you have 3 active installs in unrelated companies' accounts.

gates.name: Developer test account / own portal install
gates.unlocks: OAuth install of your Projects app into your own HubSpot account and developer test accounts.
limits: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; refresh before expiry, because a 401 is not a reliable signal to refresh
The installing user must be a Super Admin, or have Marketplace Access plus the permission for each requested scope group
Developer test accounts do not count toward install caps

gates.name: Private distribution (allowlisted accounts) or unlisted Marketplace-distribution app
gates.unlocks: Installs by invited customer accounts with no HubSpot review.
limits: Private OAuth app: up to 10 allowlisted accounts (100 customer portals if the app is created in a Solutions Partner portal)
Marketplace-distribution app before listing: up to 25 installs, not counting developer test accounts (applies to apps on platform 2025.2+)
Static-token apps: 1 standard account plus up to 10 developer test accounts
Unlisted or unverified apps show a warning at install; the user must type 'I accept the risk' to connect (not shown for Tech Partner Program members)
Without a verified domain the install page shows an 'unverified' banner; with one, it shows a 'not reviewed' banner

Rate limit: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account for Marketplace OAuth apps (the certification page says 100); private apps get 100-190 per 10 seconds and 250k-1M requests per day depending on tier
gates.time_to_reach: Same day (Marketplace distribution needs Begin publishing and a signed AUP first)

gates.name: HubSpot Marketplace listing (optional certification later)
gates.unlocks: Unlimited installs with no warning screen on the install page.
limits: At least 3 active, unique installs in production accounts not affiliated with you, with successful activity in the past 30 days
Manual review by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team; only one app can be in review at a time
Certification is a separate, optional step: it needs 6 months listed, 60 active installs, a security questionnaire, a verified domain and a demo video, and must be renewed every 2 years
gates.time_to_reach: First review response within 10 business days; up to 60 days in total, plus time to get 3 active installs in unrelated companies' accounts

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account, then log in at app.hubspot.com/developer. Apps are managed in the app under Development > Projects, which requires a login.
gotchas: The findings don't confirm whether a free developer account is enough or whether you need a paid seat.

steps.title: Scaffold a Projects app with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI, then create a project app. When prompted for distribution, choose Marketplace if you might ever go beyond 10 accounts, or private for an allowlisted set of accounts. When prompted for auth, choose OAuth, not static token.
gotchas: A static token removes redirectUrls and limits the app to one account, so it can't be used with Composio's multi-account OAuth.
You can start with private distribution and switch to Marketplace later without breaking existing installs.
Don't use legacy (non-Projects) public or private apps: creating them is being removed, and pre-Projects public apps became unsupported on September 15, 2026.

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the top-level app-hsmeta.json auth block, set redirectUrls to Composio's callback URL. In requiredScopes, list only the scopes your agent actually uses. Put scopes tied to specific HubSpot products in optionalScopes or conditionallyRequiredScopes.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: auth.requiredScopes
values.value: Minimal set, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.contacts.write, crm.objects.companies.read, crm.objects.deals.read

gotchas: Production redirect URIs must use https.
Optional scopes are dropped if the installing portal doesn't have that product, so lower-tier accounts can still install.
The 'oauth' scope is added to every app by default; you don't need to declare it.

steps.title: Upload the project and copy the credentials
steps.detail: Run hs project upload. Then open the app under Development > Projects, go to the Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret. Any later change to redirectUrls also needs another hs project upload.
gotchas: If the secret leaks, rotate it on the Auth tab. The old secret stops working immediately, so update Composio at the same time.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a HubSpot auth config that uses your own OAuth app. Paste in the Client ID and Client secret, and set the scopes to exactly match requiredScopes and optionalScopes in app-hsmeta.json. Don't keep Composio's long default scope list.
gotchas: Composio's defaults include legacy scopes (tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content, sales-email-read) and settings.users.write. Requesting scopes your app doesn't declare or doesn't need can make installs fail.

steps.title: Connect your own HubSpot account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, sign in with a Super Admin user, approve the scopes, and confirm a test API call works. Composio refreshes the 30-minute access tokens using the refresh token.
gotchas: Non-admin users need Marketplace Access plus the permission for every requested scope group (e.g. Import for crm.import), or the install fails.
To force install into one specific portal, put its account ID in the URL: /oauth/{accountId}/authorize.

steps.title: Open installs to invited accounts
steps.detail: For a private app, allowlist up to 10 customer accounts (100 if built in a Solutions Partner portal). For a Marketplace-distribution app, open the Distribution tab, click Begin publishing and sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy. Until you do, the app only installs in developer test accounts; after that, it can be installed in up to 25 accounts.
gotchas: Users of an unlisted app see an unverified-app warning and must type 'I accept the risk' before connecting.

steps.title: Verify your domain
steps.detail: Add the TXT record HubSpot gives you to your domain's DNS. This shows your domain on the install screen instead of the 'unverified' banner. Verification is required for certification.
steps.est_time: 10 min active; usually done within 1 hour, up to 48 hours
gotchas: You get one verified domain per developer account, shared by all its apps, and HubSpot re-checks it regularly.

steps.title: Get 3 active installs in unrelated companies' accounts
steps.detail: Before you can submit a listing, at least 3 unique production HubSpot accounts that aren't affiliated with your organization must have the app installed and show successful app activity within the past 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare listing materials
steps.detail: Draft live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages, a support contact, and public setup documentation (no login required) that covers install, connect, configure, use, disconnect and uninstall, including the scope approval screen. Also prepare an install button URL, pricing that matches your website, and a Shared data table that lists every object in your scopes.
gotchas: Objects you request with both read and write scopes must be listed as bi-directional.
Listing text must be specific to the integration. Write HubSpot with a capital H and S, and don't combine 'Hub' or 'HubSpot' with your app name or logo.

steps.title: Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the Marketplace listing from your developer account and agree to the Marketplace Terms and the Technology Partner Program Agreement. The app must use OAuth as its only auth method, and its public app ID must match its OAuth client ID.
gotchas: Only one app can be in review at a time; HubSpot automatically rejects any others you submit meanwhile.
Apps on a developer platform version announced as unsupported can't be listed.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team sends an initial review within 10 business days. The full feedback loop should take no more than 60 days from when they share feedback. Incomplete listings are rejected or stay in Draft.

requirements.item: OAuth (not a static token) for any app installed in more than one account
requirements.detail: Apps meant for multiple accounts or for the Marketplace must use OAuth.
Store the expires_in value (1800 seconds) and refresh before expiry; HubSpot says a 401 is not a valid signal to refresh. Composio handles this when it holds the tokens.
The installing user must be a Super Admin, or have Marketplace Access plus the permission for every scope group the app requests.
Required (Distribution tab > Begin publishing) before a Marketplace-distribution app can be installed outside developer test accounts.
Production redirect URIs must use https.
Production accounts not affiliated with your organization, with successful activity in the past 30 days.

requirements.item: Live ToS, Privacy Policy, support contact, setup docs, install URL
requirements.detail: All must be live; setup docs must be public with no login and cover the full lifecycle, including disconnect and uninstall.
Every requested scope must be used and listed in the Shared data table; remove any extras.

requirements.item: AI connectors: user-level permissions or HubSpot MCP Server
requirements.detail: To be listed, an AI connector app must require user-level permissions (added in developer platform 2026.09) or be built with HubSpot's MCP Server.

Listed for 6+ months, 60+ active installs, security questionnaire, verified domain, Uninstall App API, stable public APIs only, success rate above 95%, demo video, and no asking users to paste codes or tokens. Renew every 2 years.

scopes.effect: Standard CRM scopes. Each object you request must appear in the listing's Shared data table; objects with both read and write scopes must be listed as bi-directional.
Not allowed for agent-tool listings or in app cards for listing. Reported to be Enterprise-only. Leave them out if you plan to list.
Non-Super-Admin installers also need the Import permission, or the install fails.

Included in Composio's default list. Admin-level scopes can block non-admin users from installing, and a community report says the block can persist even after you remove the scope. Leave it out unless you need it.
Legacy scopes; HubSpot recommends migrating to granular scopes. They are in Composio's defaults, but it's unverified whether new Projects apps accept them.
Added to every app by default; you don't need to declare it.

blockers.symptom: Installs fail after 25 accounts (or 10 for a private app)
blockers.cause: Unlisted Marketplace-distribution apps (platform 2025.2+) are capped at 25 installs; private OAuth apps are capped at 10 accounts, or 100 in a Solutions Partner portal.
blockers.fix: Get your Marketplace listing approved to remove the cap, or build the private app in a Solutions Partner portal for up to 100 customer portals.

blockers.symptom: App can't be installed in any customer account, only in developer test accounts
blockers.cause: The Acceptable Use Policy hasn't been signed for a Marketplace-distribution app.
blockers.fix: On the Distribution tab, click Begin publishing and sign the AUP.

blockers.symptom: Non-admin users can't approve the install
blockers.cause: The app requests a scope the user has no permission for, or that only admins can grant. Scopes are stored per app and user, so the block can persist even after you remove the scope.
blockers.fix: Install with a Super Admin, or remove admin-level scopes and grant users Marketplace Access plus the matching permissions.

blockers.symptom: Users see an 'unverified app' warning and must type 'I accept the risk'
blockers.cause: Since March 23, 2026, HubSpot shows this for unlisted apps that its Ecosystem Quality team hasn't reviewed.
blockers.fix: Verify your domain to soften the banner. Listing the app, or joining the Tech Partner Program, removes the confirmation step.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected for an AI agent or connector
blockers.cause: The app doesn't require user-level permissions, isn't built with HubSpot's MCP Server, or requests sensitive data scopes.
blockers.fix: Move to developer platform 2026.09, require user-level access (or use the MCP Server), and remove sensitive scopes.

blockers.symptom: Listing or certification rejected because of classic CRM cards
blockers.cause: Classic CRM cards aren't allowed for listing or certification and must be migrated to App Cards by October 31, 2026.
blockers.fix: Migrate to App Cards before you submit.

blockers.symptom: Old app can't be listed or will stop working
blockers.cause: Pre-Projects public apps became unsupported on September 15, 2026 (enforcement in September 2027), and unsupported platform versions can't be listed.
blockers.fix: Build a new Projects-based app, or migrate the old one, on a supported platform version.

blockers.cause: Only one app can be in review at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the current review to finish before submitting another app.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is fine for early testing against your own portal or a few accounts. Switch to your own Projects app when you need your own branding or verified domain, control over scopes, or a Marketplace listing, or when you need installs beyond what a shared app allows. Composio's defaults include legacy and admin-level scopes, so trim them to match your app-hsmeta.json. In HubSpot, set redirectUrls to the callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

open_questions: Rate limits conflict: 110 vs 100 requests per 10 seconds per installing account for Marketplace OAuth apps. Throttle to 100 to be safe until this is confirmed.
Per-app daily limits for Marketplace OAuth apps were not stated; only the private-app tables were found.
Not confirmed whether a free developer account is enough to create Projects apps, or whether a paid seat is needed.
Eligibility for the Solutions Partner and Technology Partner programs (which raise the private cap to 100 and skip the unverified-install dialog) was not confirmed.
The scopes reference and the Projects 'working with OAuth' page could not be fetched, so scope tiers and admin-only scopes are partly unverified.
Refresh-token lifetime and revocation rules were not found.
Not confirmed whether Projects apps accept Composio's default legacy scopes (tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content, sales-email-read) or settings.users.write.
The exact UI for allowlisting accounts on a private-distribution app was not documented in the findings.
Unclear whether the 6-month and 60-install thresholds apply only to certification; the listing page itself requires only 3 installs.
The classic CRM card migration deadline is October 31, 2026, two days after today's date, and is sourced from a community post. Check it if your app uses CRM cards.
